abstract: Maintains spectrum interference mitigation and baseline noise floor records
system_message:
You are Radio frequency engineering lead (RFE). The radio frequency engineering lead (RFE) evaluates candidate observatory locations for the Southern Submillimeter Array, maintaining spectrum interference mitigation status and baseline noise floor records across candidate receiver bands, as well as data backhaul network telemetry metrics.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains spectrum interference mitigation and baseline noise floor records（RFQ）
information_points.content:
RFE-RFQ-XY4：For the Q3 2024 survey period at Chajnantor North Terrace, baseline radio interference suppression was not active across the 30 km exclusion perimeter, and the maximum peak radio frequency noise floor across the 30 GHz to 950 GHz receiver windows was -110 dBm.
RFE-RFQ-KRE：For the Q2 2024 survey period at Chajnantor North Terrace, baseline radio interference suppression was active across the 30 km exclusion perimeter, and the maximum peak radio frequency noise floor across the 30 GHz to 950 GHz receiver windows measured -110 dBm.
RFE-RFQ-M8J：For the Q2 2024 survey period at Cerro Toco Saddle, baseline radio interference suppression was active across the 30 km exclusion perimeter, and the maximum peak radio frequency noise floor across the 30 GHz to 950 GHz receiver windows was -102 dBm.
RFE-RFQ-8FM：For the Q2 2024 survey period at Pampa la Bola Plateau, baseline radio interference suppression was active across the 30 km exclusion perimeter, while the maximum peak radio frequency noise floor across the 30 GHz to 950 GHz receiver windows measured -110 dBm.

information_points.title: Telemetry transmission（FIBER）
information_points.content:
RFE-FIBER-DE5：At Chajnantor North Terrace, the optical fiber backbone latency from the site boundary to the central correlator facility is 14 ms under synthetic full-load data streaming.
RFE-FIBER-74Y：At Cerro Toco Saddle, the optical fiber backbone latency along the proposed link to the central correlator facility is 8 ms under full-load conditions.
RFE-FIBER-7PX：At Pampa la Bola Plateau, the optical fiber backbone latency measured along the run to the central correlator facility is 22 ms during synthetic full-load testing.
